name: Mythology
description: Greek, Roman, Norse and other myths, gods and heroes.

lessons.title: The Greek Olympians
lessons.body:
The twelve **Olympians** lived on Mount Olympus. Quiz bowl often asks for the **Roman name** too.

| Greek | Roman | Domain | Symbol |
|---|---|---|---|
| Zeus | Jupiter | King of the gods, sky | Thunderbolt, eagle |
| Hera | Juno | Queen, marriage | Peacock |
| Poseidon | Neptune | Sea | Trident |
| Athena | Minerva | Wisdom, war strategy | Owl |
| Apollo | Apollo | Sun, music, prophecy | Lyre |
| Artemis | Diana | Hunt, moon | Bow |
| Ares | Mars | War | Spear |
| Aphrodite | Venus | Love | Dove |
| Hermes | Mercury | Messenger | Winged sandals |
| Hephaestus | Vulcan | Fire, forge | Hammer |

**Hades** (Roman Pluto) ruled the underworld but lived there, not on Olympus.
keyFacts: Zeus is called Jupiter by the Romans.
Athena was born fully grown from Zeus’s head.
Poseidon carries a trident.
Hermes wears winged sandals and guides souls to the underworld.
Apollo and Artemis are twins.

lessons.title: Creation, Titans and Prometheus
lessons.body:
Greek myths begin with **Chaos**, an empty void. From it came **Gaia** (Earth), who married **Uranus** (Sky). Their children were the twelve **Titans**.

## The Titans take over
- The Titan **Cronus** overthrew his father Uranus with a sickle.
- Afraid his own children would do the same, Cronus **swallowed** each one at birth.
- His wife **Rhea** saved baby **Zeus** by giving Cronus a **stone wrapped in a blanket** instead. Zeus grew up in secret on the island of **Crete**.
- Zeus forced Cronus to throw up his brothers and sisters. The gods then beat the Titans in a ten-year war called the **Titanomachy**.

## Punishments
- **Atlas**, who fought against Zeus, had to hold up the **sky** forever.
- **Prometheus** stole **fire** from the gods (hidden in a fennel stalk) and gave it to humans. Zeus chained him to a rock where an **eagle** ate his liver every day, and it grew back every night.
- To punish humans, Zeus sent **Pandora**, the first woman, with a jar (often called a box). She opened it and released all the evils of the world. Only **hope** stayed inside.

**Tip:** the Roman name for Cronus is **Saturn**, which is why Saturn's moons are named after Titans like Titan and Rhea.
keyFacts: Gaia is the Earth; Uranus is the Sky.
Cronus swallowed his children; Rhea tricked him with a stone.
Atlas was punished by holding up the sky.
Prometheus stole fire for humans; an eagle ate his liver.
Hope remained inside Pandora's jar.

lessons.title: The Underworld and Famous Monsters
lessons.body:
**Hades** ruled the underworld, the land of the dead.

## The journey of the dead
- Souls were ferried across the **River Styx** by **Charon**, who demanded a coin as payment.
- The gate was guarded by **Cerberus**, a **three-headed dog**.
- Good souls went to the **Elysian Fields**; the wicked were punished in **Tartarus**. **Sisyphus** must roll a boulder uphill forever, and **Tantalus** stands in water he can never drink (that's where "tantalize" comes from).

## Persephone and the seasons
Hades kidnapped **Persephone**, daughter of the harvest goddess **Demeter**. Because Persephone ate **pomegranate seeds** in the underworld, she must return there for part of each year. While Demeter mourns, plants die. That is how the Greeks explained **winter**.

## Monsters to know
| Monster | Description |
|---|---|
| **Medusa** | Gorgon with snakes for hair; turns people to stone |
| **Minotaur** | Half man, half bull; lived in the Labyrinth |
| **Cyclopes** | One-eyed giants who made Zeus's thunderbolts |
| **Sphinx** | Asked travelers a riddle; solved by **Oedipus** |
| **Hydra** | Grew two heads for each one cut off |
| **Chimera** | Lion, goat and serpent parts; breathed fire |
keyFacts: Charon ferries souls across the River Styx.
Cerberus is a three-headed dog guarding the underworld.
Persephone ate pomegranate seeds, which explains the seasons.
Sisyphus rolls a boulder uphill forever.
Oedipus solved the riddle of the Sphinx.

lessons.title: Greek Heroes and Their Quests
lessons.body:
Greek heroes were often children of gods who faced monsters on dangerous quests.

- **Heracles** (Roman **Hercules**), son of Zeus, performed **Twelve Labors** for King Eurystheus. They included killing the **Nemean Lion**, slaying the many-headed **Hydra**, cleaning the **Augean stables** in one day by redirecting two rivers, and capturing **Cerberus**.
- **Perseus** cut off the head of **Medusa**, a Gorgon with snakes for hair whose gaze turned people to stone. He used a polished shield from Athena to see her reflection. The winged horse **Pegasus** sprang from Medusa's neck. Perseus then rescued **Andromeda** from a sea monster.
- **Theseus**, prince of Athens, killed the **Minotaur** (half man, half bull) in the **Labyrinth** on Crete. Princess **Ariadne** gave him a ball of thread to find his way out. His father **Aegeus** leaped into the sea when Theseus forgot to change his black sails to white, giving the **Aegean Sea** its name.
- **Daedalus** built the Labyrinth. He made wax wings to escape Crete, but his son **Icarus** flew too close to the sun and fell.
- **Jason** led the **Argonauts** on the ship *Argo* to find the **Golden Fleece**, helped by the sorceress **Medea**.
- **Orpheus**, a musician, went to the underworld for his wife **Eurydice** but lost her when he looked back.
keyFacts: Heracles (Hercules) performed Twelve Labors, starting with the Nemean Lion.
Perseus beheaded Medusa using a mirrored shield.
Theseus used Ariadne's thread to escape the Labyrinth after killing the Minotaur.
Icarus flew too close to the sun on wax wings.
Jason sailed on the Argo to find the Golden Fleece.

lessons.title: The Trojan War and the Odyssey
lessons.body:
The **Trojan War** is the most famous story in Greek myth. The poet **Homer** told parts of it in two epic poems, the **Iliad** and the **Odyssey**.

## How the war began
At a wedding, **Eris**, goddess of discord, threw a **golden apple** marked "for the fairest." Hera, Athena and Aphrodite all claimed it. The Trojan prince **Paris** chose **Aphrodite**, who rewarded him with **Helen**, the most beautiful woman in the world. But Helen was married to **Menelaus**, king of Sparta, so the Greeks sailed to **Troy** to get her back.

## The heroes
- **Achilles**: the greatest Greek warrior. His mother **Thetis** dipped him in the River Styx, making him invulnerable everywhere except his **heel**.
- **Hector**: Troy's greatest warrior, killed by Achilles. Achilles was later killed by an arrow from Paris.
- **Agamemnon**: leader of the Greek army, brother of Menelaus.
- **Cassandra**: a Trojan princess who could see the future, but no one believed her.

After ten years, **Odysseus** came up with the **Trojan Horse**: soldiers hid inside a giant wooden horse, which the Trojans pulled into the city.

## The Odyssey
Odysseus spends **ten more years** getting home to **Ithaca**. He blinds the Cyclops **Polyphemus** after saying his name is "Nobody," sails past the **Sirens** while tied to the mast, and escapes the witch **Circe**. At home, his wife **Penelope** and son **Telemachus** have waited for him.
keyFacts: Paris gave the golden apple to Aphrodite and won Helen.
Achilles could only be hurt in his heel.
Odysseus thought up the Trojan Horse.
Odysseus told the Cyclops Polyphemus his name was 'Nobody'.
Penelope is Odysseus's wife; Ithaca is his home.

lessons.title: Roman Myths and Legends
lessons.body:
The Romans borrowed most of their gods from the Greeks but added their own legends about the founding of Rome.

- **Romulus and Remus**: twin sons of the war god **Mars**. They were left in a basket on the **Tiber River** and nursed by a **she-wolf**. Romulus killed Remus in an argument and founded **Rome**, traditionally in **753 BCE**.
- **Aeneas**: a Trojan hero who escaped the burning city of Troy carrying his father Anchises. The poet **Virgil** told his story in the **Aeneid**. On the way to Italy, Aeneas fell in love with **Dido**, queen of Carthage. The Romans saw Aeneas as their ancestor.
- **Janus**: a god with **two faces**, one looking forward and one back. He ruled doorways and beginnings, and **January** is named for him. He had no Greek version.
- **Vesta**: goddess of the hearth. The **Vestal Virgins** kept her sacred fire burning.

## Roman names in our world
- **Planets**: Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn and Neptune are Roman gods.
- **Months**: January (Janus), March (Mars), June (Juno).
- **Words**: "cereal" comes from **Ceres** (Greek Demeter); "volcano" from **Vulcan**.
- **Cupid** is the Roman Eros; **Bacchus** is the Roman Dionysus.
keyFacts: Romulus and Remus were raised by a she-wolf; Romulus founded Rome.
Virgil wrote the Aeneid about the Trojan hero Aeneas.
Janus has two faces; January is named for him.
Ceres, goddess of grain, gives us the word 'cereal'.
Vestal Virgins tended the sacred fire of Vesta.

lessons.title: Norse Gods
lessons.body:
Norse myths come from Scandinavia and were written down in Iceland in works called the **Eddas**.

- **Odin**, the all-father, gave up an eye to drink from Mímir’s well of wisdom. His ravens are Huginn and Muninn.
- **Thor**, god of thunder, wields the hammer **Mjölnir**.
- **Loki** is a trickster who causes the death of **Baldur** with a dart of mistletoe.
- The world tree **Yggdrasil** connects the nine worlds, including **Asgard** (home of the gods) and **Midgard** (home of humans).
- Warriors who die in battle may go to **Valhalla**, chosen by the **Valkyries**.
- **Ragnarök** is the final battle that destroys the world.

Days of the week honor these gods: Wednesday (Odin/Woden), Thursday (Thor), Friday (Frigg).
keyFacts: Thor’s hammer is named Mjölnir.
Odin traded an eye for wisdom.
Yggdrasil is the world tree connecting nine worlds.
Loki caused Baldur’s death using mistletoe.
Ragnarök is the end of the world in Norse myth.

lessons.title: Egyptian Gods
lessons.body:
Ancient Egyptian gods were often shown with **human bodies and animal heads**.

| God | Look | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **Ra** | Falcon head with sun disk | Sun god; sails across the sky in a boat |
| **Osiris** | Green skin, wrapped like a mummy | God of the dead and the afterlife |
| **Isis** | Throne-shaped headdress | Magic and motherhood; wife of Osiris |
| **Horus** | Falcon | Sky god; son of Osiris and Isis |
| **Set** | Strange animal head | Chaos, deserts and storms |
| **Anubis** | Jackal | Mummification and guiding the dead |
| **Thoth** | Ibis bird | Writing and wisdom |
| **Bastet** | Cat | Protection and the home |

## The story of Osiris
Jealous **Set** killed his brother **Osiris** and scattered the pieces of his body across Egypt. **Isis** found the pieces and brought him back to life, and Osiris became ruler of the underworld. Their son **Horus** fought Set and lost an eye, which was healed. The **Eye of Horus** became a symbol of protection.

## Judgment of the dead
In the afterlife, **Anubis** weighed a person's **heart** against the **feather of Ma'at**, goddess of truth. A heart heavier than the feather was eaten by the monster **Ammit**. Spells to help the dead were written in the **Book of the Dead**.
keyFacts: Ra is the Egyptian sun god.
Set killed his brother Osiris; Isis brought him back.
Anubis has a jackal's head and oversees mummification.
The heart of the dead was weighed against the feather of Ma'at.
Thoth, god of writing, has the head of an ibis.

lessons.title: Myths and Legends Around the World
lessons.body:
Quiz bowl also asks about myths from many other cultures.

- **Mesopotamia**: the **Epic of Gilgamesh**, one of the oldest written stories. King **Gilgamesh** of Uruk and his friend **Enkidu** kill the monster Humbaba. After Enkidu dies, Gilgamesh searches for immortality and meets **Utnapishtim**, who survived a great flood by building a boat.
- **India (Hindu)**: **Brahma** the creator, **Vishnu** the preserver (who comes to Earth as avatars like **Rama** and **Krishna**), and **Shiva** the destroyer. **Ganesha**, son of Shiva, has an **elephant's head** and removes obstacles.
- **Japan**: the sun goddess **Amaterasu** hid in a cave and plunged the world into darkness until the other gods lured her out with a mirror and a dance.
- **China**: the giant **Pangu** hatched from a cosmic egg and separated sky and earth. **Sun Wukong**, the **Monkey King**, travels with a monk in *Journey to the West*.
- **Mesoamerica**: the Aztec feathered serpent **Quetzalcoatl**. In the Maya book **Popol Vuh**, the **Hero Twins** play a ballgame against the lords of the underworld, Xibalba.
- **Britain**: **King Arthur** pulled a sword from a stone and received **Excalibur** from the Lady of the Lake. He ruled from **Camelot** with the **Knights of the Round Table**, advised by the wizard **Merlin**. His knights searched for the **Holy Grail**.
keyFacts: Gilgamesh was king of Uruk; his friend was Enkidu.
Ganesha, with an elephant's head, removes obstacles.
Amaterasu is the Japanese sun goddess.
Sun Wukong is the Monkey King of Journey to the West.
King Arthur's sword is Excalibur; his court was Camelot.

tossups.question: This deity won a contest by giving an olive tree to a city. She was born fully armored from her father’s head, and her sacred animal is the owl. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of wisdom for whom Athens is named.
This god owns a belt of strength and iron gloves. His goats Tanngrisnir and Tanngnjóstr pull his chariot, and he wields the hammer Mjölnir. For 10 points, name this Norse god of thunder.
This god's son Triton blows a conch shell. He created the first horse, and when angry he caused earthquakes. For 10 points, name this Greek god of the sea who carries a trident.

This god was born on the island of Delos and drives a chariot across the sky. He gave prophecies through the oracle at Delphi and plays the lyre. For 10 points, name this Greek god of music and the sun, the twin of Artemis.

This god stole Apollo's cattle when he was one day old and invented the lyre from a tortoise shell. He carries a staff called the caduceus and wears winged sandals. For 10 points, name this messenger of the gods.

This god was thrown off Mount Olympus and landed on the island of Lemnos, leaving him lame. His workshop was under a volcano, and he was married to Aphrodite. For 10 points, name this Greek blacksmith god of fire.

This goddess turned the hunter Actaeon into a stag after he saw her bathing. With her twin brother, she killed the children of Niobe, and her Roman name is Diana. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon.

This Titan's brother Epimetheus married Pandora. He hid a gift for humans inside a fennel stalk, and as punishment an eagle ate his liver every day. For 10 points, name this Titan who stole fire from the gods.

This Titan fought against Zeus and was punished by being made to hold up the sky. A book of maps is named for him, as is an ocean, the Atlantic. For 10 points, name this Titan who carries the heavens on his shoulders.

This figure's husband ignored his brother's warning not to accept gifts from Zeus. She was made by Hephaestus from clay and given a container she was told never to open. For 10 points, name this first woman in Greek myth, who let all the evils into the world.

This Titan was given a stone wrapped in swaddling clothes by his wife Rhea. He used a sickle to overthrow his father Uranus, and he swallowed his own children. For 10 points, name this Titan father of Zeus, known to the Romans as Saturn.

This goddess was the mother of the Cyclopes and the Titans. She is the first being to emerge from Chaos in many tellings, and she married the sky god Uranus. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess who personifies the Earth.
This creature was the final labor of Heracles, and Orpheus put it to sleep with music. It has a serpent's tail and three heads. For 10 points, name this dog that guards the gates of the underworld.

This goddess's mother made the crops stop growing while searching for her. She ate pomegranate seeds, so she must spend part of each year below the earth. For 10 points, name this daughter of Demeter who became queen of the underworld.

This figure was the son of Erebus and Nyx in some stories. The Greeks placed a coin called an obol in the mouths of the dead to pay him. For 10 points, name this ferryman who carries souls across the River Styx.

This creature had the body of a lion and the head of a woman, and it guarded the city of Thebes. It asked what walks on four legs in the morning, two at noon and three in the evening. For 10 points, name this monster whose riddle was solved by Oedipus.

This king tricked Death by chaining him up, so no one could die. As punishment in Tartarus, he must push a boulder up a hill, only to have it roll down again forever. For 10 points, name this king of Corinth.

This hero strangled two snakes sent by Hera while he was still a baby. He wore the skin of the Nemean Lion and cleaned the Augean stables in one day. For 10 points, name this son of Zeus who completed Twelve Labors.
This character's father made him wings of feathers and wax to escape from King Minos. He ignored warnings, flew too close to the sun, and fell into the sea. For 10 points, name this son of Daedalus.

This hero received a sword and sandals hidden under a rock by his father Aegeus. Ariadne gave him a ball of thread so he could escape the Labyrinth. For 10 points, name this Athenian hero who killed the Minotaur.
This hero was sent by King Polydectes to fetch a monster's head. He used a mirrored shield from Athena and saved Andromeda from a sea monster. For 10 points, name this Greek hero who beheaded Medusa.

This hero showed up wearing only one sandal, which frightened King Pelias. He sowed dragon's teeth and was helped by the sorceress Medea. For 10 points, name this leader of the Argonauts who found the Golden Fleece.
This musician sailed with the Argonauts and drowned out the Sirens' song. He charmed Hades with his lyre, but lost his wife Eurydice by looking back at her. For 10 points, name this legendary singer.
This object was inscribed "for the fairest" and thrown into a wedding feast by Eris. Paris awarded it to Aphrodite. For 10 points, name this golden fruit that led to the Trojan War.

This warrior refused to fight after Agamemnon took his prize, Briseis. He returned after Hector killed his friend Patroclus. His mother Thetis dipped him in the River Styx, holding him by the heel. For 10 points, name this greatest Greek warrior of the Trojan War.

This man's dog Argos recognizes him after twenty years, and he wins a contest by shooting an arrow through twelve axe heads. He outwits the Cyclops Polyphemus. For 10 points, name this king of Ithaca, the hero of a Homer epic.

This Trojan princess was given the gift of prophecy by Apollo. When she refused him, he cursed her so that no one would believe her. For 10 points, name this daughter of King Priam who warned that Troy would fall.
This woman tells her many suitors she will choose one once she finishes weaving a shroud for Laertes. Each night she secretly unravels her work. For 10 points, name this faithful wife of Odysseus.

These two brothers were saved by a woodpecker and a shepherd named Faustulus. After they were nursed by a she-wolf, one killed the other in an argument over where to build a city. For 10 points, name these twins, one of whom founded Rome.

This god's temple in Rome had doors that stood open in times of war and closed in times of peace. He has two faces, looking to the past and the future. For 10 points, name this Roman god of doorways for whom January is named.

This hero visits the underworld with the Sibyl to see his dead father Anchises. He abandons Queen Dido of Carthage to fulfill his destiny in Italy. For 10 points, name this Trojan hero of an epic by Virgil.

This goddess's priestesses served for thirty years and were punished if they let a flame go out. Her Greek counterpart is Hestia. For 10 points, name this Roman goddess of the hearth whose sacred fire was tended by six virgins.

This Roman goddess searched for her daughter Proserpina. Her Greek counterpart is Demeter, and her name gives us an English word for breakfast grains. For 10 points, name this Roman goddess of agriculture.

This god hung himself on a tree for nine nights to learn the secret of runes. His ravens are Huginn and Muninn, and he gave up an eye to drink from Mimir's well. For 10 points, name this chief Norse god.

This god's children include the wolf Fenrir, the serpent Jormungandr and the eight-legged horse Sleipnir. He tricked the blind god Hodr into throwing mistletoe at Baldur. For 10 points, name this Norse trickster god.

This tree has an eagle at its top and a dragon named Nidhogg chewing at its roots. A squirrel runs up and down it carrying insults, and it connects the nine worlds. For 10 points, name this world tree of Norse mythology.

During this event, Heimdall will blow the horn Gjallarhorn and the wolf Fenrir will swallow Odin. Thor and the Midgard Serpent will kill each other. For 10 points, name this final battle at the end of the world in Norse myth.
This god's daily journey began each morning when he was reborn. At night he traveled through the underworld in a boat and fought the serpent Apep. For 10 points, name this Egyptian sun god.
This god oversaw the weighing of the heart against a feather. Embalmers sometimes wore masks of his head, which was that of a jackal. For 10 points, name this Egyptian god of mummification.

This god was tricked into lying in a beautiful coffin, which was then sealed and thrown into the Nile. His body was later cut into pieces by his brother Set. For 10 points, name this green-skinned Egyptian god who became king of the dead.

This god lost an eye fighting his uncle Set, and his eye became a protective symbol. The pharaoh was seen as his living form, and he has the head of a falcon. For 10 points, name this son of Osiris and Isis.
This god is credited with inventing hieroglyphics and recording the results when hearts are weighed. He has the head of an ibis. For 10 points, name this Egyptian god of writing and wisdom.

This god lost his original head when his father, who did not recognize him, cut it off. He rides a mouse and is prayed to at the start of new projects. For 10 points, name this elephant-headed Hindu god, the remover of obstacles.
This king received the sword Excalibur from the Lady of the Lake. Mordred fatally wounded him, and he was taken to the island of Avalon. For 10 points, name this legendary British king of Camelot.

This hero builds a gate from the cedar wood of a forest guarded by Humbaba. A snake steals the plant of youth he was given by Utnapishtim. For 10 points, name this king of Uruk, the hero of a Mesopotamian epic.

This goddess was offended by her brother Susanoo, the storm god, and hid in a cave. The gods lured her out with a mirror and a dance, bringing back light. For 10 points, name this Japanese sun goddess.

This character was born from a stone and can leap 108,000 li in a single somersault. He fought the armies of heaven and was trapped under a mountain by the Buddha. For 10 points, name this Monkey King of Journey to the West.
